knowledge_graph.title: Leukoencephalopathy with vanishing white matter
knowledge_graph.description: Leukoencephalopathy with vanishing white matter is an autosomal recessive neurological disease. The cause of the disease are mutations in any of the 5 genes encoding subunits of the translation initiation factor eIF2B: EIF2B1, EIF2B2, EIF2B3, EIF2B4, or EIF2B5.

text_blocks.snippet: White matter disease refers to a group of disorders that affect the brain's white matter, which is composed of nerve fibers (axons) and the myelin sheaths that protect and insulate them. These diseases can manifest in various ways, ranging from subtle cognitive changes to severe neurological deficits.

list.title: What it is:
list.snippet: White matter disease encompasses a wide range of conditions, including genetic disorders, vascular issues (like strokes), and inflammatory or infectious diseases.

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: The disease affects the white matter, which is crucial for communication between different brain areas and the spinal cord.
